consumer_protection.case_name: Manjeet Singh vs National Insurance Company Ltd
consumer_protection.facts: Singh purchased car insurance from National Insurance. After accident, company rejected claim citing policy breach (driver unlicensed at accident). Singh had valid license at policy inception, held current license, but temporary suspension during accident due to traffic violation. Company argued technicality justifies full rejection.

timeline.event: Complaint filed in District Consumer Commission

consumer_protection.court_reasoning: Supreme Court held that minor policy breaches do not justify complete claim rejection if breach is not fundamental to risk assessment. Insurance company has duty to act in good faith. Technicality cannot override consumer protection principle.
consumer_protection.relief_granted: ₹4,50,000 (75% of insured amount) + ₹50,000 compensation + 9% interest per annum from date of accident
consumer_protection.evidence_details: Policy documents, premium receipts, police FIR, medical reports, garage repair estimates, insurance correspondence
risk_factors: Policyholder had valid reason for suspension
consumer_protection.key_takeaways: Insurance companies cannot use technical breaches to reject entire claims. Good faith principle applies. Consumer Protection Act protects policyholders from unfair claim rejection.

consumer_protection.case_name: Priya Sharma vs Samsung India Electronics
consumer_protection.facts: Priya purchased Samsung refrigerator for ₹75,000. After 8 months, compressor failed. Within warranty period but company demanded ₹15,000 service charge claiming 'physical damage'. Priya had never physically damaged product. Company refused warranty claim.

timeline.event: Complaint filed in District Consumer Commission

sections: Sale of Goods Act Section 14 - Warranty
consumer_protection.court_reasoning: Compressor failure within warranty period is manufacturing defect, not physical damage. Company must prove physical damage with evidence. Warranty cannot be voided without proof. Consumer acted reasonably.
consumer_protection.relief_granted: ₹75,000 full refund + ₹10,000 compensation for harassment + ₹5,000 legal costs
consumer_protection.evidence_details: Purchase invoice, warranty card, original packaging (no damage), photos of product, service denial email, product manual
consumer_protection.key_takeaways: Warranty claims for manufacturing defects must be honored. Companies cannot impose charges for inherent defects.

consumer_protection.case_name: Rajesh Kumar vs Spring Meadows Hospital
consumer_protection.facts: Child suffered oxygen deprivation during birth at Spring Meadows Hospital, resulting in permanent cerebral palsy. Hospital staff failed to monitor fetal distress. Parents paid ₹3,00,000 for delivery.
consumer_protection.court_reasoning: Medical negligence proven. Hospital failed in duty of care. Permanent disability of child requires lifetime care. Medical staff should have detected distress signals.
consumer_protection.key_takeaways: Medical negligence must be proven with expert opinion. Hospitals liable for permanent injuries from negligent care.

consumer_protection.case_name: D.C. Sharma vs DDA - Double Allotment
consumer_protection.facts: Sharma paid ₹50,00,000 for DDA plot in 1997. Later discovered same plot allotted to another person in 1995 due to DDA's administrative error. DDA had double allotted same property.
consumer_protection.court_reasoning: DDA's administrative negligence caused double allotment. Sharma entitled to compensation at current market value reflecting escalation.
consumer_protection.relief_granted: ₹2,50,00,000 (current market value) OR alternate plot + ₹50,00,000 compensation
consumer_protection.key_takeaways: Government entities liable for administrative errors. Market value compensation applicable for delayed discovery.
